text.p: British supermarket group J. Sainsbury Plc has received authorisation from the Bank of England to operate its planned joint venture Sainsbury's Bank with Bank of Scotland, a spokeswoman said.
The company is still on target to launch the service, which would be based on telebanking, in the first quarter of this year, she added.
Sainsbury and Bank of Scotland announced their plans for the bank, which will be 55 percent owned by the supermarket group, in October 1996.
Sainsbury, which is Britain's second largest grocer in terms of market share, said then it would kick off with Classic and Gold Visa cards along with account and card-based services.
The bank will have its headquarters in Edinburgh, Scotland.
Sainsbury is the only one of the big four supermarkets to plan banking operations, although market leader Tesco offers customers an account which pays interest.
Third-placed Safeway announced on Monday plans for an interest-paying account with a card which can be used at outlets displaying the Electron sign with Abbey National.
All three already have nationwide loyalty cards while ASDA is testing schemes in some of its stores.
